narrative.overview:
A single-page Korean CV laid out like a magazine feature on warm A4 paper. The masthead carries the identity — a folio rule with contacts, the name set huge in MaruBuri, and the headline as a pull-quote hung on a brick quotation mark — followed by a one-column lead opened with a brick drop cap. Sections open under newspaper double rules; every entry sits on an editorial grid with a 31mm margin column for periods, margin-note links, or a short heading.

Ornament stays typographic: quote mark, drop cap, double rules, timeline dots, brick list dashes. No photos, icons, cards, skill bars, or fills. The owner chose this direction (variant E) on 2026-10-08 over the earlier plain version, which felt too simple. The same warm sheet is the screen page and the printed page.
keyCharacteristics: One A4 sheet in warm paper (#faf6ee); screen padding equals the @page margins, so web and PDF share a 178mm content box.
MaruBuri for name, pull-quote, section titles, entry names, margin headings, and decks; Pretendard for everything else.
Warm ink ladder plus a single brick accent (#9c3b25) for editorial ornaments and margin-note links.
Editorial grid: 31mm margin column + 10mm gutter + text column; dated sections become a timeline.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Brick #9c3b25 is the only chromatic colour: quote mark, drop cap, timeline dots, list dashes, Skills separators, margin-note links, hover and focus. Hierarchy otherwise steps down the ink ladder.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Every text colour is ≥ 4.5:1 on paper (ink 15.5, secondary 9.0, muted 5.6, brick 6.4). Rule, rule-strong, and accent-line draw lines only.

rules.name: The Quiet Cross-Reference Rule
rules.body: In-page links (href^="#") such as [Buzzvil] are muted ink with a faint rule underline; content links keep the accent-line underline. Repeated wayfinding must not out-shout citations.

rules.name: The pt-Only Rule
rules.body: Every font size is pt, never px or rem, so screen and PDF share physical sizes.

rules.name: The Keep-All Rule
rules.body: word-break: keep-all and hanging-punctuation govern Korean breaking; text-wrap: pretty on prose, balance on the pull-quote; <mark> phrases never wrap.

rules.name: The One Source, Two Outputs Rule
rules.body: Screen sheet and printed page share every token; the PDF is the browser's print of the page, never a generated file. Print CSS only sets @page and paginates. html uses print-color-adjust: exact so paper tone, marks, and dots print with Background graphics off, and @page declares empty @top-left/@bottom-left margin boxes to suppress the browser's print header and footer.

rules.name: The Two-Item Break Rule
rules.body: Headings stay with their first body block; list items never split; a list breaks only with at least two items on each side. Entries themselves stay breakable so a long section can start at a page foot.

rules.name: The Single Shadow Rule
rules.body: The sheet's screen-only lift is the only shadow; inside the sheet, separation is rules and whitespace.

dos: Do keep every size in pt and the A4 geometry in mm tokens shared by .sheet and @page.
Do reserve brick for the editorial ornaments and margin-note links.
Do keep repeated in-page references quiet (muted ink, faint underline).
Do keep the pagination rules — heading with first block, no lone first or last bullet — when changing layout.
Do print the page from the browser (Save as PDF) and look at every page after a spacing change.
donts: Don't add photos, icons, skill bars, badges, cards, or decorative backgrounds.
Don't add a second accent colour or tint section bands.
Don't make whole entries or sections break-inside: avoid; it pushes long sections to the next page and leaves empty bands.
Don't set the about lead in narrow multi-columns; Korean phrases split badly.
